pezzi.36: No data leaves the machine, and no bill per token. What it asks for in return is memory, and memory is a sum you do beforehand, not afterwards.
pezzi.38: A model takes up memory in proportion to its parameters and to the number of bits each weight is stored in. That is where you start if you want to know whether a machine can cope, before downloading twenty gigabytes.
pezzi.48: the context cache, which grows with the length of the conversation
pezzi.50: The table I use when someone asks me whether their computer is enough. Model names change every month: the classes and the arithmetic do not.
pezzi.76: The browser reports little, for privacy reasons: number of processors, graphics card and a memory figure stuck at 8 GB. The rest you set yourself, and the sum is arithmetic anyone can check.
pezzi.100: Quantisation does not degrade everything in the same way, and the first part to give way is not the one people usually watch.
pezzi.104: Small loss on text, visible on maths and code
pezzi.106: Tool calls start to break: wrong format, invented parameters
pezzi.108: For an agent I count memory at Q5 or Q6, not at Q4
pezzi.110: It is not an ideological question. It is a question of where the data sits, how much work there is and how much quality is needed.
pezzi.112: The company’s data cannot leave the building
pezzi.113: High volumes of simple, repetitive tasks
pezzi.114: It has to work without a network too
pezzi.115: Predictable cost: you pay for the machine, not for the token
pezzi.118: Very long contexts on modest hardware
pezzi.119: Few requests a day: the machine sits idle
pezzi.120: Nobody to update and keep an eye on the system
pezzi.121: The sum that always goes wrong
pezzi.122: A model that fits in memory but leaves no room for context is not slow: it stops.
pezzi.124: A local model does not match a frontier model on hard problems, and saying otherwise is dishonest. What it does well is bounded, repetitive work, with the data staying inside. Most of the systems I build use both, and the choice is made step by step.
